questions.sub: Origin and migration of the Mizo people
questions.question: According to widely accepted oral tradition, the Mizo people trace their earliest legendary origin to emergence from a place/rock called:
questions.explanation: Mizo oral tradition holds that their ancestors emerged from a place called Chhinlung (Sinlung), often associated with a legendary site in present-day China, before their long migration.

questions.sub: Origin and migration of the Mizo people
questions.question: The Mizo people are generally believed to belong to which broader ethnic/linguistic group?
questions.explanation: The Mizo, along with other Kuki-Chin-Mizo groups, belong to the Tibeto-Burman linguistic and ethnic family, having migrated from the Chin Hills/Myanmar region into present-day Mizoram.

questions.sub: Traditional Mizo society, chieftainship and Zawlbuk
questions.question: In traditional Mizo village society, the village chief was known as:
questions.explanation: In traditional Mizo society, the village chief was called 'Lal', who administered the village with the help of a council of elders (Upa).

questions.sub: Traditional Mizo society, chieftainship and Zawlbuk
questions.question: The 'Zawlbuk' in traditional Mizo village life was primarily:

options.B: A bachelors' dormitory that trained unmarried young men and served as a defence post
options.C: A sacred worship hall for the priest

questions.explanation: The Zawlbuk was a communal bachelors' dormitory where unmarried young men lived, received informal training in discipline, warfare and social duties, and helped defend the village.

questions.sub: Advent of the British and annexation of the Lushai Hills
questions.question: The Lushai Hills (present-day Mizoram) came under formal British control following which military expedition?
questions.explanation: The Lushai Expedition of 1871-72, launched after Lushai raids on British tea gardens and the abduction of Mary Winchester, was a key step leading to British annexation of the Lushai Hills, formally completed in 1890-95.

questions.sub: Advent of the British and annexation of the Lushai Hills
questions.question: The Lushai Hills District was formally constituted and placed under British administration as part of which province?
questions.explanation: After annexation in the 1890s, the Lushai Hills District was administered as part of the province of Assam under British rule.

questions.sub: Christian missionaries, literacy and social change
questions.question: Which two pioneer Christian missionaries are credited with arriving in the Lushai Hills in 1894 and establishing the foundation of modern education and the Mizo written script?

options.B: F. W. Savidge and J. H. Lorrain
options.C: J. N. Farquhar and C. F. Andrews

questions.explanation: F. W. Savidge and J. H. Lorrain, pioneer Welsh/British missionaries, arrived in Aizawl on 11 January 1894 and are regarded as founders of modern education, the Mizo alphabet/script and literature; 11 January is observed as Missionary Day in Mizoram.

questions.sub: The Mizo National Front movement and the 1966 uprising
questions.question: The Mizo National Famine Front, precursor to the Mizo National Front, was formed in 1959-60 in response to which crisis?

options.D: Severe drought in the Chittagong Hill Tracts

questions.explanation: The Mizo National Famine Front was formed in 1959 to coordinate relief during the Mautam famine caused by bamboo flowering and the resulting rodent infestation destroying crops; perceived government inaction fuelled the later demand for a separate Mizo state.

questions.sub: The Mizo National Front movement and the 1966 uprising
questions.question: Who led the Mizo National Front (MNF) and declared independence, triggering the armed uprising against the Indian government on 1 March 1966?
questions.explanation: Laldenga, founder-leader of the Mizo National Front, declared independence and launched the armed insurgency (Operation Jericho) on 1 March 1966, leading to two decades of insurgency.

questions.sub: Mizoram Peace Accord 1986 and attainment of statehood 1987
questions.question: The Mizoram Peace Accord, which ended the two-decade-long insurgency, was signed between the Government of India and the Mizo National Front in which year?
questions.explanation: The Mizoram Peace Accord was signed on 30 June 1986 between the Government of India, represented by Home Secretary R. D. Pradhan, and Laldenga of the MNF.

questions.sub: Mizoram Peace Accord 1986 and attainment of statehood 1987
questions.question: Mizoram was granted full statehood as the 23rd state of the Indian Union on which date?
questions.explanation: Mizoram became the 23rd state of India on 20 February 1987, under the State of Mizoram Act, 1986, following the Peace Accord; it had earlier been a Union Territory since 1972.

questions.sub: Districts, administrative structure and local government of Mizoram
questions.question: Which district of Mizoram shares a trade border town, Zokhawthar, with Myanmar and is a key border trade point?
questions.explanation: Zokhawthar, a village in Champhai district, is a major India-Myanmar border trade point located on the Tiau river.

questions.sub: Mizo festivals, dances, dress, cuisine and folklore
questions.question: Which of the following is a traditional Mizo harvest/agricultural festival?
questions.explanation: Chapchar Kut is one of the most important and popular traditional Mizo festivals, celebrated after jhum (shifting cultivation) clearing operations, marking the beginning of spring.

questions.sub: Mizo festivals, dances, dress, cuisine and folklore
questions.question: The famous Mizo bamboo dance, in which dancers step between crossed bamboo staves to rhythmic beats, is known as:
questions.explanation: Cheraw, popularly called the bamboo dance, is one of the oldest and most iconic traditional Mizo dances, performed with pairs of horizontal bamboo staves.

questions.question: Who signed the 1986 Mizoram Peace Accord on behalf of the Mizo National Front and went on to become the first Chief Minister of the State of Mizoram?
questions.explanation: Laldenga, MNF leader, became the first Chief Minister of Mizoram after statehood in 1987 following the Peace Accord he signed in 1986; Ch. Chhunga had earlier served as Chief Minister of the Union Territory formed in 1972.
